comparisons.peer_topic: Commercial loan modification program metrics (2024 vs 2023)
comparisons.peer_summary: In 2024, term extensions increased the weighted-average life of impacted loans by 1.7 years compared to 1.6 years in 2023, while the weighted-average duration of deferred payments was 9 months for both years; deferral periods typically ranged from 8 to 24 months.
comparisons.comparison: Both JPMorgan and Bank of America disclose the specific impact of loan modifications on loan metrics, particularly term extensions. JPMorgan reports that financial distress modifications (FDMs) in residential real estate extended the weighted-average loan life by 15 years, with modifications predominantly consisting of term extensions and interest rate reductions. Similarly, Bank of America discloses that term extensions granted to troubled borrowers increased the weighted-average life of impacted loans by 1.7 years in 2024. While both track the extension of loan life as a primary metric of modification concessions, JPMorgan's disclosed extension period (15 years) is significantly longer than Bank of America's (1.7 years), and JPMorgan provides specific details on interest rate reductions (from 7.53% to 5.44%) which are not quantified in the comparable Bank of America text.

sentences.text: For the year ended December 31, 2024, retained residential real estate FDMs were $206 million.

The financial effects of the FDMs, which were predominantly in the form of term extensions and interest rate reductions, included extending the weighted-average life of the loans by 15 years, and reducing the weighted-average contractual interest rate from 7.53% to 5.44% for the year ended December 31, 2024.
Term extensions granted increased the weighted-average life of the impacted loans by 1.7 years during 2024 compared to 1.6 years in 2023.

comparisons.peer_topic: Loan Modification Practices for Distressed Borrowers
comparisons.peer_summary: The Firm may modify loan terms for borrowers experiencing financial difficulties through mechanisms such as interest rate reductions, principal forgiveness, term extensions, and other concessions.
comparisons.comparison: Both JPMorgan and Morgan Stanley disclose the types of concessions made in loan modifications for borrowers facing financial difficulties. JPMorgan specifies that its retained residential real estate FDMs were 'predominantly in the form of term extensions and interest rate reductions.' Morgan Stanley broadly states that the Firm may modify terms for borrowers experiencing financial difficulties through mechanisms including 'interest rate reductions, principal forgiveness, term extensions and other-than-insignificant payment deferrals.' Both companies identify term extensions and interest rate reductions as common modification tools, though Morgan Stanley also explicitly lists principal forgiveness and payment deferrals, whereas JPMorgan's specific disclosure highlights the magnitude of term extensions and rate cuts in its residential real estate portfolio.
